from.place: proof step 2: refinement of an fppf covering of an affine object by affine objects

title: Affine refinement of an fppf covering
statement: Let U = Spec(A) be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\{T_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ be an fppf covering family [def-pc-fppf-site], that is, each $T_i \to U$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, and the family is jointly surjective, $\bigcup_{i\in I}\operatorname{im}(T_i\to U)=U$ (as in the fppf coverings of Stacks Tag 021L). There are finitely many indices i(1), ..., i(m), affine open subschemes V_j contained in T_{i(j)}, and factorizations $V_j \to T_{i(j)} \to U$ such that each $V_j \to U$ is fppf and the images of the V_j jointly cover U.

source.place: Stacks Project, Tag 021P, Lemma 34.7.4 (affine refinement of an fppf covering); used in Tag 021V, Lemma 34.7.11

proof.text: For each member T_i of the given fppf covering, take an affine-open covering of T_i using lem-pc-fppf-affine-open-cover. Each chosen affine open V_{i,alpha} is contained in T_i. The composite V_{i,alpha} \to T_i \to U is flat and locally of finite presentation because these properties hold for the open immersion and for T_i \to U and are stable under composition, hence it is fppf.

The images of all the V_{i,alpha} in U are open: the composites are flat and locally of finite presentation, so this follows from lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open. They jointly cover U because the family {T_i \to U} is jointly surjective by the hypothesis of the statement (the cited def-pc-fppf-site lists only flatness and local finite presentation) and the affine opens V_{i,alpha} cover each T_i by lem-pc-fppf-affine-open-cover.

Write U=\operatorname{Spec}(A). The principal opens D(f) form a basis, and if they cover U then the ideal generated by the corresponding f's is the unit ideal; hence finitely many already generate 1 (equivalently, a finite subcover exists), so U is quasi-compact in the sense of def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme. Apply this to the open cover from the preceding step, relabel its finitely many members as V_1, ..., V_m, and write i(j) for the corresponding original index. Each V_j is affine and contained in T_{i(j)}, each composite V_j \to U is fppf, and their images jointly cover U, which is the required refinement.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finite_fppf_affine_open_refinement {U : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine U] {I : Type v} (T : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, T i ⟶ U) (hf : Presieve.ofArrows T f ∈ fppfPrecoverage U) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n → I) (V : ∀ j, (T (i j)).Opens), (∀ j, IsAffineOpen (V j)) ∧ Presieve.ofArrows (fun j ↦ (V j).toScheme) (fun j ↦ (V j).ι ≫ f (i j)) ∈ fppfPrecoverage U
